hooks.title: 600 M ISLAND LAKE

beats.text: Six hundred meters of pink water, and the ocean is just past the sand.
Paint? Pollution? What turns a salt lake pink?
Scoop it into a container, and it stays pink.
End to end, it's almost two Eiffel Towers long.
It sits on Middle Island, off Western Australia.
The color is believed to come from a tiny organism, Dunaliella salina.
Scientists found its DNA here, with salt-loving bacteria.
A dense woodland of paperbark and eucalyptus rings the lake.
Next target: an African valley below sea level. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: Lake Hillier is a saline lake about 600 metres long on Middle Island, off the south coast of Western Australia, and its pink colour stays the same even in a container. The colour is believed to come from the organism Dunaliella salina, which the Extreme Microbiome Project found in a metagenomic analysis of the lake.
